review_notes: I read the whole file. I compared its definitions with Mathlib's group-action API (Algebra/Group/Action/Basic.lean and End.lean) and with the downstream file Algebra/Torsor/Basic.lean. The torsor classes themselves are a bundled structure with a subtraction field, so I did not treat them as competing with IsPretransitive or free-action predicates. `smulConst` and `constSDiv` use the torsor division, so they are genuinely torsor-specific. `pointReflection` has no apparent existing counterpart. The one clear duplicate is `Equiv.constSMul`, with `constSMulHom` in Basic.lean as a consequence. The one remaining uncertainty is how many external call sites use `Equiv.constVAdd` and `Equiv.constSMul`. AffineEquiv.lean and IsometricSMul.lean use `Equiv.constVAdd` and `IsometryEquiv.constVAdd`. I did not count every use. Any migration would need to keep explicit-argument conventions (the `P` argument) compatible.

findings.excerpt:
def constSMul (v : G) : Equiv.Perm P where
  toFun := (v • ·)
  invFun := (v⁻¹ • ·)
findings.problem: `Equiv.constSMul P v` is the same permutation as the existing `MulAction.toPerm v : Equiv.Perm P`, with `toFun` the same `(v • ·)` and `invFun` the same `(v⁻¹ • ·)`. The `AddAction.toPerm` counterpart covers `constVAdd`. It is stated only for `[Group G] [Torsor G P]`, but its proof uses only the `MulAction` structure, so the torsor hypothesis adds nothing. The file therefore adds a parallel API for 'the permutation induced by a group element'. In `Torsor/Basic.lean`, `constSMul_one`, `constSMul_mul` and `constSMulHom` repeat what `MulAction.toPerm_one` and `MulAction.toPermHom` already give. `constSMulHom` has the same shape as `MulAction.toPermHom`. The `coe_constSMul` simp lemma competes with the `simps` lemmas of `toPerm`, so simp normal forms and rewrites can split between the two families.
findings.proposed_change: Make `Equiv.constSMul` a thin reducible alias of `MulAction.toPerm`, keeping the explicit-`P` signature. One option is `abbrev constSMul (v : G) : Perm P := MulAction.toPerm v`, with `constVAdd` likewise an abbrev for `AddAction.toPerm`. Alternatively, deprecate it and migrate callers to `MulAction.toPerm` and `AddAction.toPerm`. Then drop `constSMul_one`, `constSMul_mul` and `constSMulHom` in favour of `MulAction.toPerm_one`, `MulAction.toPermHom` and the existing `map_mul` lemmas, or state them as aliases. If a torsor-specific name is kept, move the `[Torsor]` requirement out of it and say in the docstring that it is `MulAction.toPerm`.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical API and one set of simp lemmas for permutations induced by group actions. Torsor code and generic action code then interoperate without conversions, and there are fewer duplicated declarations to maintain.

evidence.excerpt:
def MulAction.toPerm (a : α) : Equiv.Perm β :=
  ⟨fun x => a • x, fun x => a⁻¹ • x, inv_smul_smul a, smul_inv_smul a⟩

def MulAction.toPermHom : G →* Equiv.Perm α where
  toFun := MulAction.toPerm

def constSMulHom : G →* Equiv.Perm P where
  toFun v := constSMul P v
